raw_response:
I've been growing cotton on this same land for decades. Quzhou's soil knows cotton and cotton knows me. At 63, living alone, I can't afford big experiments — I need reliable results from 4.1 mu, which is all I have. My well gives me water when I need it, and I know this land's rhythm.

Spring is coming, so I start planning now. I'll deep rotary till the field before planting — that's what I've always done to loosen the soil after winter. I use improved Bt hybrid cotton seed, been doing that since the government pushed it years back, saves me from spraying as much for bollworm. Still need to spray for aphids and spider mites though — always do, every year.

I'll put nitrogen at 20 jin per mu (about 10 kg), phosphorus base dressing, and some potash. My soil here has been worked for 40 years, it doesn't need as much as younger fields. I irrigate from my well — probably four times: once before planting, once at seedling, once at flowering, once during boll development. If it rains well I skip one.

I expect around 250 kg of seed cotton per mu. Some years better, some worse. With 4.1 mu that's about a ton of seed cotton total — enough for a single old man.
